subject: CostPilot onboarding: tuning milestones and routing fallback matrix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@costpilot.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CostPilot onboarding: tuning milestones and routing fallback matrix

Alex —

Great to kick this off. Per our discovery call, here's a proposed focused plan for the first 3 weeks that keeps cost predictability and latency SLOs front-and-center while we ramp traffic: 

1) Week 0 (this week): instrumentation + baseline capture
   - Get test API keys and 48h of representative traffic replay (we requested costpilot_kpis.csv — thanks).
   - We’ll produce a baseline token-level cost heatmap and p50/p95 latency distribution.

2) Week 1: batching & KV-prefix caching trial
   - Configure request grouping with target batch sizing heuristics (start: 8-16, adapt by latency).
   - Enable prefix KV caching for short-chat flows; measure hit-rate and tail-latency impact.

3) Week 2: quantization profile selection + routing policy
   - Test two quantization profiles on a small canary: conservative profile (higher fidelity, q8_0-like) and aggressive profile (smaller memory, q4_0-like).
   - Routing: latency-first for peak US traffic; cost-first for batch/off-peak. Define a simple fallback matrix when capacity is constrained.

Deliverables we’ll share: a one-page tuning playbook, a canary checklist, and updated milestone PDF (attached: redwood_onboard_milestones.pdf).

Questions for you to confirm before we schedule the kickoff call:
- Confirm p95 latency SLO you care about (target we discussed was ~300ms) and any absolute max latency that must not be exceeded.
- Provide expected QPS peaks and a rough hourly distribution.
- Any restricted classification of payloads we should route to private-only infra?

If that looks right I’ll assign owners and propose times for an initial 30-minute technical sync.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: costpilot_kpis.csv, redwood_onboard_milestones.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@costpilot.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: CostPilot SRE <sre@costpilot.io>
Date: 2029-09-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CostPilot onboarding: tuning milestones and routing fallback matrix

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. A few data points from our side to help you shape the canary: 
- Expected peak QPS: ~60 sustained bursts (we see spikes to 120 during marketing pushes).
- Average QPS: ~22.
- Average token length: ~120 tokens, heavy long-tail up to 800 tokens on analysis flows.
- p95 target: 300ms; p99 ideally <900ms but we can accept higher during known maintenance windows.

We are very concerned about quality regressions from aggressive quantization — accuracy on core prompt sets is business-critical. We’d like an automatic rollback if quality metrics on the validation set degrade >2% relative to baseline.

I’ve looped in our SRE. We can provide a service account and a staging cluster for canaries. Also attaching a quick list of procurement/legal flags — we’ll send a fuller doc if needed.

Cheers,
Alex Johnson
Head of Product | CostPilot
alex.j@costpilot.io

Attachments: (none in this message)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@costpilot.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-10-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CostPilot onboarding: tuning milestones and routing fallback matrix

Alex / Team —

Thanks for the numbers — that helps. A few technical bullets to align expectations: 

- Batching: start with a dynamic batching window capped at 25ms targeting batch sizes 8–16. For your 120-token average we expect token-limited batching to be important; we’ll instrument median token-per-batch.

- KV-prefix caching: enable for intents/short responses only initially. We’ll flag analysis flows (long token) as non-cacheable. Expect ~15–25% hit-rate on short flows based on similar customers.

- Quantization profiles: we recommend testing two profiles in parallel on canary:
   * fidelity-priority profile (higher internal FP bits, minimal accuracy loss) — labeled as INTERNAL-PROFILE-A
   * economy-priority profile (more aggressive memory/computation reduction) — labeled as INTERNAL-PROFILE-B
  We will run an A/B of both against your validation set and compute delta on the 12 critical prompts you provided. If delta >2% on any important metric we auto-fail that profile and revert.

- Routing: define policy entries in the routing table: 
   * route(latency_first) -> model_variant_highperf in us-east
   * route(cost_first) -> model_variant_quantized during off-peak EU/US night
   * fallback -> smaller base model (quantized) with warning hooks to ops

Action items from our side before the kick: 
1) Provide a service account and staging cluster access by EOD Wednesday.
2) Share the 12 validation prompts and expected labels (or scoring function).
3) Confirm which flows are allowed to hit cached results.

I’ll prepare the tuning runbook and canary checklist and drop it in the drive link you’ll get.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: redwood_canary_checklist.md (will be uploaded to drive)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@costpilot.io>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@costpilot.io>, CostPilot SRE <sre@costpilot.io>
Date: 2029-10-01T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CostPilot onboarding: tuning milestones and routing fallback matrix

Monica / Marissa —

All sounds good. Quick replies to the action items: 
1) Service account + staging cluster access: I’ll have our SRE open a service account and share the kubeconfig by EOD tomorrow.
2) Validation prompts: Priya will attach the 12 prompts and expected scoring in a follow-up.
3) Cacheable flows: we confirm short-help/intents and template responses only. Analysis and billing queries should be non-cacheable.

Procurement note: before we commit to any reserved capacity we need a ballpark monthly cost delta between the economy-priority profile and fidelity-priority profile at your recommended batch sizes. Can you provide a short estimate sheet? I’ve attached a list of procurement questions — would appreciate a concise answers doc.

Also — can you add a short section in the runbook around regression validation (what to check after switching quant profiles)? That will help my PM and QA sign off.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachment stub: procurement_questions.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@costpilot.io>, Priya Rao <priya@costpilot.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-10-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CostPilot onboarding: tuning milestones and routing fallback matrix

Team —

Summarizing and assigning next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Decisions agreed
- Canary strategy: run A/B of INTERNAL-PROFILE-A (fidelity) vs INTERNAL-PROFILE-B (economy) against 12 validation prompts. Auto-fail if >2% delta on key metrics.
- Routing matrix: latency-first for peak US traffic, cost-first during off-peak, fallback to smaller quantized base model with ops notifications.
- Caching: enabled for short-help and templated responses only. Analysis/billing flows excluded.

Owners & deadlines
- Alex / CostPilot SRE: share kubeconfig + staging cluster access by 2029-10-03 EOD. (Alex)
- Priya: deliver validation prompts and expected labels by 2029-10-03. (Priya)
- Monica: deliver the tuning runbook + canary checklist and a 1-page regression validation section by 2029-10-04. (Monica)
- Rishi & Karthik: provide a concise cost delta estimate for the two quant profiles with recommended batch sizing by 2029-10-05. (Rishi, Karthik)

Next meeting: 30-minute technical sync scheduled for 2029-10-07 10:00am PT to review canary checklist and gating criteria. Invite to follow.

Immediate asks from CostPilot: please upload the procurement_questions.docx and the 12 validation prompts to the shared drive link so we can start building the automated checks.

If anyone needs to escalate sooner, reply-all or ping me.

Thanks everyone — excited to get the canary started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
